rejected_attempts.reason: The new native enumeration fixture initially retained a const cursor while calling its non-const read method. Corrected fixture ownership to a mutable cursor for enumeration; the probe still accepts const shared ownership. Strict compilation was preserved. No tests were run after this failed build.

GCC rejected a copied range-loop pair in the new Linux native fixture under -Werror=range-loop-construct. Changed the fixture loop to const reference, retaining every assertion and strict warnings. The driver stopped before CTest; final corrected source passed normal and sanitizer runs.

The initial failed fixture build had successfully compiled the new core and deterministic fixture; it was not used to run tests. Final logs identify the corrected compiled fixtures and links.

Windows final build/test took 5.700/3.130 s after its successful initial expanded target build. Per-host manifests agree on all 134 exported inputs; the unchanged test-host hash is additionally recorded. Native/core output hashes and case markers establish freshness, not elapsed time.

native_qualification.positive_native_scope: Linux ext4 scratch filesystem; native type/flags checked by fixtures
native_qualification.macos: Lexical relation, unavailable native policy and retained-directory refresh
native_qualification.windows: Lexical relation, unavailable native policy and retained-directory refresh

guarantees: A potentially usable rule requires two live location observations through one retained directory, with native identity qualified against the cursor context and relevant filesystem/flag fields in agreement. An unqualified first observation is not retried.

Linux extended-filesystem type 0xef53 and successful inode flags with casefold and filename-encryption bits clear qualify bytewise POSIX-name matching. Different filesystem/family, encryption/casefold, field errors and changed/unqualified context do not become positive policy evidence. Native-header constants are asserted.

Exact native units are only a lexical witness and retain unavailable directory context. A distinct relation requires a qualified policy and matching native encoding, without locale/Unicode/display conversion. Distinct names do not mean distinct objects.
Comparison limits precede scans and bound each native component in bytes, including UTF-16 byte accounting. No truncation or rewritten name is returned. No filesystem I/O occurs during comparison.

Refresh uses the retained directory after original-name replacement, old reports remain independent, and final native-owner retirement belongs on workers. Cancellation returns no partial probe; query exceptions release private staging.
limitations: These are observed name rules, not an execution-time collision proof, native name acceptance, absence, object inequality, permission, capacity, mount confinement or a namespace snapshot. Current occupants and parent/rule qualification must be checked again for operation execution.

Darwin/Windows and other Linux filesystem policies remain unqualified. Casefold and fscrypt filename-encrypted directories remain unqualified even with loaded keys. Native positive fixtures cover the Linux ext4 scratch filesystem; no native ext2/ext3, casefold, encrypted-directory or other-driver fixture qualification is claimed.
The two reports cannot exclude intermediate or later rule changes. Native calls may block despite cooperative cancellation. The component budget is not a process-memory or filesystem-name/path limit.
Available(probe) does not imply an available rule. Exact lexical relation can remain available while native context/rules are unavailable; callers must preserve that distinction.

No macOS LeakSanitizer coverage is claimed. Full cross-platform name/collision handling, complete capability/preservation assessment, large-view indexes, UI/worker and execution integration remain open in WP-01. WP-02..08 remain required.
